scope: all Bedrijfsgeheugen/Powerhouse material delivery and governance work
problem: A material change can be merged yet remain incompletely institutionalized if its learning, skills, documentation, ledger and applicable post-merge readback are not all closed in the same canonical lineage.
root_cause: Borging was sometimes treated as a follow-up documentation action rather than a first-class delivery obligation with its own protected-main and readback closure.
rule: A request to borg/log/document/update skills becomes material writeback. Close it through canonical learning + relevant skill + Powerhouse docs/ledger + policy attachment when reusable + protected merge + current-main ancestry proof + applicable production or non-deployment readback.
supersession_behavior: When main moves, do not chase stale heads or treat cancellation as failure/success by itself. Prove the borging commit is an ancestor of the newer current main and require terminal readback on that current lineage.
deployment_applicability: For docs/governance-only changes, Production Release Readback may explicitly mark deployment not applicable. For runtime/public-surface changes, exact provider identity and functional browser/readback remain mandatory.
prevention: never write material borging directly to main
never stop at PR or merge
never treat a cancelled superseded verifier as functional proof
make the reusable rule discoverable to the next chat/agent through skill projection and canonical policy

evidence.production_readback: Protected merge + current-main ancestry + applicable Production Release Readback are required before terminal closure.
